source.title: An Adaptive and Momental Bound Method for Stochastic Learning
source.authors: Jianbang Ding; Xuancheng Ren; Ruixuan Luo; Xu Sun

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance across optimizers, using image-classification and language-modeling experiments relevant to V4; the study focuses on AdaMod stability, not directly on the generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy or perplexity for SGDM, Adam, and AdaMod. The Transformer BLEU table is flattened and optimizer-to-value assignments cannot be recovered confidently; cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out image-classification accuracy for momentum SGD and adaptive optimizers, bearing on V4. It uses decoupled weight decay for adaptive methods and does not document a matched tuning budget, so it does not precisely reproduce V4's limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors primarily conclude that AdaMod bounds extreme adaptive learning rates, stabilizes training, and improves over Adam especially on DenseNet and Transformer. They acknowledge remaining gaps to SGDM, report AdaMod beating SGDM on CIFAR-10 DenseNet, and find only a slight improvement over Adam on Penn Treebank.
record.recipe_differences: Compares Adam, AdaMod, and SGDM in task-specific experiments; all adaptive methods use decoupled weight decay. Adam uses warmup for Transformer experiments, while AdaMod does not. The CIFAR comparisons use 3 random seeds.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and dataset/model change the relative test performance; the text reports different outcomes across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Penn Treebank.

fits_no_version.finding: On Penn Treebank, AdaMod has slightly lower test perplexity than Adam: means 70.76 versus 70.95, with no SGD comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bounding Adam's adaptive learning rates can slightly improve word-level language-model performance relative to Adam.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer experiments compare Adam with and without warmup against AdaMod; they report divergence without Adam warmup and improved BLEU with AdaMod.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive learning-rate bounds can stabilize Transformer training and replace warmup in the tested recipes.

record.problems: The study is not designed as a controlled generalization comparison; it evaluates AdaMod against task-specific baselines. Hyperparameter tuning equivalence is not reported. Results are based on 3 random seeds for the image and Penn Treebank experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Transformer BLEU results in Table 2 and accuracy-curve values in Figures 4–7 are not extracted because the supplied text flattens the relevant table layout or gives plots without recoverable numerical values. The table's optimizer-to-BLEU assignments cannot be confidently mapped.

Equal or better training performance is stated for AdaMod on ResNet, but is not established numerically for Adam in the supplied text.

missing.what: The text explicitly states that AdaMod has better ResNet training performance despite worse test accuracy than SGDM. The existing rows contain only test accuracy, omitting evidence for V4's training-versus-held-out distinction.
missing.locator: Image Classification, ResNet paragraph following Tables 3–5

record.verdict_notes: All extracted table values are correct. Comparisons between two adaptive optimizers alone do not test V4. Decoupled weight decay is applied throughout the adaptive-method experiments, so these results cannot isolate its recovery effect. Figure-only results and Transformer BLEU were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
